# Inside the AI Chip War: From Nvidia’s Dominance to Intel’s Turmoil | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 28

First listed: 2025-10-06 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Inside the AI Chip War: From Nvidia’s Dominance to Intel’s Turmoil | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fphcOSPgHtM) - 2025-10-06
- [Substack: Inside the AI Chip War: From Nvidia’s Dominance to Intel’s Turmoil | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 28](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/inside-the-ai-chip-war-from-nvidias-622) - 2025-10-06

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Stacy Rasgon separates the AI semiconductor boom from the weaker analog cycle, stresses NVIDIA's software ecosystem, and remains cautious about AMD and Intel. Eisman tests funding and return assumptions without declaring AI useless or predicting an imminent collapse. The clearest direct correction is that the announced NVIDIA investment in OpenAI was staged. The guest's claim that outsiders do not use TPUs is contradicted by Google's documented multi-year Anthropic relationship.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

### 033. Intel's foundry strategy incurred enormous losses before securing substantial outside leading-edge customers; 18A internal product ramps do not prove external foundry success.

**Mixed** | Stacy Rasgon | explanation | major

[Source at 51:45-54:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fphcOSPgHtM&t=3105s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Large historical losses and still-limited external revenue support the distinction. 2026 process and revenue progress prevent treating the thesis as proof that nothing ever improves.

Assessment test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

Further verification: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

- [Intel 2024 Form 10-K](https://www.intc.com/filings-reports/annual-reports/content/0000050863-25-000009/0000050863-25-000009.pdf) (2025-01-31): Foundry operating loss was $13.408 billion in 2024, including substantial impairments, accelerated depreciation, ramp and startup costs. It is not all cash burn or all idle capacity.
- [Intel Q3 2026 Form 10-Q](https://www.intc.com/filings-reports/all-sec-filings/content/0000050863-26-000191/intc-20260926.htm) (2026-10-30): 18A-P entered risk production in June 2026. Q3 external foundry revenue $411 million versus $32 million, mainly a nonrecurring contract, and internal advanced-node volumes increased. External revenue is not necessarily recurring leading-edge wafer volume.

## Framework and tools

- Distinguish economic usefulness from returns on invested capital.
- Separate cyclic digestion from a failed structural thesis.
- Treat capex cuts as potentially late signals and monitor underlying use.
- Do not infer equity value from TAM times assumed share.
- Distinguish liquidity support from operating competitiveness.
- Demand differentiated customer preference rather than a second-source narrative.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- AI versus analog semiconductor cycle
- GPU versus ASIC share and workload economics
- OpenAI funding commitments versus cash
- CoWoS/HBM supply-chain indicators
- TI inventory days and backlog visibility
- Intel foundry losses and external customer milestones

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman interviews Stacy Rasgon. Most sector calls belong to Rasgon; Eisman probes returns and valuation and accepts the staged-investment correction.
- Opening montage duplicates later discussion.
- All 2009 caption lines were read, including a reread of an initially truncated middle segment.
- Guest numbers and management targets are not automatically Eisman forecasts.
- Transcript occasionally garbles chip names and semiconductor terms.
- The guest immediately self-corrects the lithography size direction; it is not a substantive mistaken thesis.
